chunks: Abu al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Tabari narrated to us, he said: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Karrash narrated to us, he said: Our master Anas narrated to us, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Modesty and faith are all in one horn; when one of them is removed, the other follows it - meaning that whoever modesty does not restrain from the ugly (bad deeds) in what is between him and the people, he will not be restrained from the ugly in what is between him and his Lord, Exalted and Majestic; and whoever does not feel modesty before Allah, Exalted and Majestic, and openly displays the ugly, he has no religion -.

key_terms.الْحَيَاءُ: Modesty/Shyness (a virtue and barrier against sin)
key_terms.قَرْنٌ: Horn (metaphor for a single unit or container)

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between modesty and faith in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq places this narration in the 'Chapter of Rare Meanings' to highlight the profound ontological link between internal character (hayā') and theological belief (īmān). The text elucidates that modesty acts as a comprehensive shield; its absence in social conduct signals a deeper deficiency in one's relationship with God, ultimately resulting in the loss of 'dīn' (religion/faith). This reflects the Shia emphasis on the unity of inner piety and outward behavior as indicators of true faith.
